summary: The Phoenix proposal aims to enhance AI routing resilience by addressing timeouts and unavailable providers without altering production behavior or fabricating votes. The acceptance tests and bounded design are well-defined, ensuring that safety flags remain false and that the system behaves as expected under various conditions.
top_technical_reasons: The proposal includes robust acceptance tests that ensure timeouts and malformed reviews are handled correctly.
The design preserves provider lineage during fallback attempts, maintaining transparency in decision-making.
Quorum calculations are based solely on valid completed verdicts, preventing erroneous approvals.
candidate_safety: Safety flags remain false, indicating that the proposal does not introduce new risks to the production environment.

next_experiments.hypothesis: Implementing a short-prompt retry will reduce the number of timeouts experienced.
next_experiments.change: Introduce a short-prompt retry mechanism before falling back to alternative providers.
next_experiments.metric_gate: Measure the reduction in timeout occurrences over a defined period.
next_experiments.why_it_is_informative: This experiment will provide insights into the effectiveness of retries in improving response times and reducing reliance on fallback providers.

next_experiments.hypothesis: Explicitly recording timeout/error/rate-limit statuses will improve error handling.
next_experiments.change: Enhance the logging mechanism to capture detailed statuses for timeouts and errors.
next_experiments.metric_gate: Analyze the frequency and types of errors recorded before and after implementation.
next_experiments.why_it_is_informative: Understanding the nature of errors will help refine the routing logic and improve overall system resilience.

data_or_label_risks: No data or label risks identified, as the proposal maintains existing safety flags and does not alter production behavior.
